_doc: The laws of each realm (systems/laws.js; the Laws panel ui/actionMenu/laws.js). Each law has options; a realm's law is set on kingdom.laws (saved with the realm). Until a ruler sets one, a realm keeps its old custom: share[option] of realms hold each (a hash of the realm, the same all game). Only the ruler of a realm may change its law: each change costs changeCost.treasury from the crown's treasury and changeCost.stability of the realm's stability (folk dislike upheaval), plus the option's own stability (adopting a hard law costs more), and a law may be changed again only after cooldownDays. Every law is read by the game: privatePrisons by systems/knockout.js (a private citizen may drag the beaten off to their prison camp only where it's allowed); foreignLand by systems/lots.js (where only subjects may hold land, a stranger can't buy a lot or a house, nor rent one); punishment by systems/streetCrime.js and systems/underworld.js (arrests: fines and days in the cells) (the watch's fines and days in the cells, × fine and × jail) and by systems/knockout.js (× deter: the chance that whoever downs you finishes you or goes through your purse, and that one who hates you sets on you at home); vice by systems/gangs.js (what the gangs' gambling dens take, the crackdown they draw, and the licence the crown takes).

ai._doc: The AI realms' rulers change their laws (systems/lawCouncil.js, every everyDays). Each rule names a law, the trigger that weighs the danger (plague: the plague in, or within radius hexes of, one of the realm's towns: a town's roster sick of it, or the plague world event's town; a town's sickness record counts staleDays), the option proclaimed while it stands (on) and the one gone back to after (off). Hysteresis: the danger must stand actDays before the crown acts; it relents only once nothing is within clearRadius (wider than radius) for clearDays, and the law has held minHoldDays. The ruler's traits shift act and clear (days) and radius (hexes): the wise and the fearful act sooner and relent later; the greedy and merchant princes, who lose the trade, wait and open early. A proclamation pays the option's own stability, not the treasury, and the heralds cry it (data/chatter.json heralds law_<law>_<option>). A realm the player rules is the player's to decide.

local._doc: A town's own ordinances (Laws.localVice): settlement.ordinances.vice = 'forbidden' | 'follow', set by whoever holds the town; until then a town keeps its old custom, a hash of the town (banShare of towns ban dice and cards whatever the realm allows). A town may be stricter than its realm, never laxer.

backRooms._doc: Where gaming is forbidden (the realm's vice law, or the town's own ban: Laws.gambling) no gaming house opens: the tavern's tables, the town's Gambling Den and a tavern of yours can't run dice openly. Dice go underground, behind a legitimate front (systems/backRooms.js): a gang's den runs in the back of a real business in town (fronts), and a tavern of yours can be fitted with a hidden back room (fitCost) where its tables earn as before. Getting in: one of the gang, or a guild hand, walks in; anyone else pays the doorman (doorFee, x strangerFee for a stranger with no contact), the fee into the gang's purse. Each day you sit down there the watch may raid (raidBase + raidPerCrackdown x the town's crackdown, x boughtCaptain if the gang has bought the captain): the stakes on the table are lost, a fine (fine x the realm's punishment law) to the town's purse, and heat. A back room in your own tavern risks a raid each night (tavernRaid, the same scaling): a fine, its tables seized (seizeShare), heat.

privatePrisons.name: Private Prisons
privatePrisons.desc: May a private citizen keep a prison camp, and put those they take to work?

forbidden.label: Forbidden
forbidden.desc: Only the crown keeps prisoners. Whoever takes a captive must hand them to the watch.

allowed.label: Allowed
allowed.desc: Free folk may keep prison camps and work their prisoners. Those who set on you may drag you off to theirs.

foreignLand.name: Land for Foreigners
foreignLand.desc: May those not sworn to the realm buy building lots and houses in its towns?

open.label: Open to all
open.desc: Anyone with the coin may buy a lot or a house, or rent one.

subjects.label: Subjects only
subjects.desc: Only those sworn to the realm may buy or rent land and houses in its towns.

punishment.name: Punishment
punishment.desc: How hard the watch comes down on brawlers and worse: the fines and the days in the cells.

lenient.label: Lenient
lenient.desc: Lighter fines, shorter stays in the cells. Those who would rob or kill a fallen man fear the law less.

standard.label: Customary
standard.desc: The fines and sentences of long custom.

harsh.label: Harsh
harsh.desc: Heavy fines and long sentences. The streets are quieter; the people grumble.

mutilation.name: Mutilation
mutilation.desc: Does the realm's law take a limb for a crime? (systems/maiming.js: what the courts take — the player tried, the player as judge, the realm's own courts each week — and how the realm's folk take a hand cut off in the street.)

never.label: No limb taken
never.desc: Fines, the cells, the brand and the rope; never a hand.

thieves.label: A thief's hand
thieves.desc: A thief convicted a second time loses a hand on the scaffold. Thieves keep away; the poor mutter.

old.label: The old law
old.desc: A thief's hand on the first conviction, a cheat's ear, a slanderer's tongue. The streets are very quiet.

corporal.name: The Lash and the Iron
corporal.desc: What the courts may do to a body short of a limb or a life (systems/penalLabour.js: the player as judge, the realm's own courts each week, the player tried): the stocks only, the lash at the whipping post, or the lash and the branding iron. Harder law cows the town's thieves and sours its folk at every public punishment.

stocks.label: The stocks only
stocks.desc: A day in the pillory for the town to pelt; no lash, no iron.

lash.label: The lash
lash.desc: Flogging at the post for theft, brawling and the like. Fewer thieves; the square watches.

iron.label: The lash and the iron
iron.desc: The lash, and the court's letter burned into the cheek of a felon: a thief's T, a poacher's P. Marked folk find no honest work.

penalLabour.name: Penal Labour
penalLabour.desc: May the courts sentence a convict to hard labour for a term (systems/penalLabour.js): to a mine (yours, or the crown's: real output) or to the oars of a galley (unpaid crew, sullen and dangerous)?

none.label: No convict labour
none.desc: Convicts sit in the cells or pay; no one is worked for the crown.

mines.label: To the mines
mines.desc: Long sentences are served at the mines: ore for the crown, and many never come home.

oars.label: The mines and the oars
oars.desc: The mines, and the galley bench for the worst: oarsmen without wages for the fleet.

trialCustoms.name: Trial Customs
trialCustoms.desc: May a case be settled by another judgement than the court's: trial by combat, the hot iron, the water, the blessed bread, oath-helpers? (player/ordeals.js: your own trial, the cases before your court, your kin accused, lawsuits between Houses. The realm's faith may still forbid the ordeals.)

court.label: The court alone
court.desc: Judges and juries decide. No one may demand combat or an ordeal.

combat.label: Wager of battle
combat.desc: The accused may demand trial by combat, or clear themselves with oath-helpers. No ordeals.

ordeal.label: The church's ordeals
ordeal.desc: The hot iron, the water and the blessed bread, and oath-helpers. No combat.

old.label: The old customs
old.desc: Combat, every ordeal and oath-helpers: God decides whatever the court thinks. The lettered grumble.

torture.name: Torture
torture.desc: May a prisoner be put to the question with irons and fire? (systems/interrogation.js: what is lawful in your dungeon, and what costs you heat with the crown and the realm's regard when word gets out.)

forbidden.label: Forbidden
forbidden.desc: A prisoner may be questioned and threatened, never hurt. Whoever starves, racks or burns one has broken the law.

treason.label: For treason only
treason.desc: The irons are for those who plot against the crown and its lords: a rival House's blood, a bought man, a plotter's tool.

free.label: At the gaoler's will
free.desc: Any prisoner may be put to the question as hard as the gaoler likes. The cellars are full of screams; the people fear the crown.

vice.name: Gaming & Vice
vice.desc: Dice dens, card tables and back rooms: does the crown hunt them, wink at them, or license them?

forbidden.label: Forbidden
forbidden.desc: Dens are hunted. They take less and the watch's crackdown runs hotter wherever they open.

tolerated.label: Tolerated
tolerated.desc: The watch looks the other way, so long as nobody is killed in one.

licensed.label: Licensed
licensed.desc: Dens may trade openly for a licence: they take more, the crackdown eases, and a fifth of their take goes to the crown's treasury.

bloodSports.name: Blood Sports
bloodSports.desc: Pit fights, bear-baiting and cockfights (systems/pitFights.js): may the towns keep their pits in the open, must they pay the crown a share of the gate, or are they hunted? A town may forbid its own pit where the realm allows it (settlement.ordinances.bloodSports).

open.label: Open
open.desc: The pits fight in the open: men to first blood, to submission or to the death, the bear in his yard, the birds in their ring.

taxed.label: Taxed
taxed.desc: The pits fight openly but pay the crown a fifth of every night's gate.

banned.label: Banned
banned.desc: The pits are forbidden. They go underground, into cellars behind some honest front, and the watch raids them. The clergy are glad of it.

curfew.name: Curfew
curfew.desc: Must the streets of the realm's towns be empty after the curfew bell? (systems/nightStreets.js: townsfolk keep indoors, the watch walks its beat with lanterns and stops anyone out; a town may keep a curfew of its own where the realm keeps none.)

none.label: No curfew
none.desc: Folk come and go as they please by night.

curfew.label: Curfew
curfew.desc: From the curfew bell till dawn the streets are the watch's: anyone out is stopped, fined or jailed. Quieter nights; the taverns and the night folk grumble.

bloodPrice.name: Blood Price
bloodPrice.desc: When blood is spilt, is vengeance the kin's right, or is there a price for a life? (systems/bloodFeuds.js: the wergild tariff, who arbitrates the payment, how readily kin take silver for blood, how fast feuds cool, and how often avengers strike.)

vengeance.label: The kin's right
vengeance.desc: Blood answers blood. Kin take silver grudgingly, with no one to stand between; feuds burn long and avengers strike often.

customary.label: Customary wergild
customary.desc: A price for every rank, paid before the priest and the town council, who take a tithe of it.

crown.label: The crown's tariff
crown.desc: The crown fixes the price of a life and its justiciar sees it paid: dearer, but the kin must take it, feuds cool fast, and the crown takes its fee.

pestilence.name: Pestilence
pestilence.desc: When sickness goes round a town, do its gates stay open to travellers and trade, or are they shut? (systems/illness.js: a sick town under quarantine passes a case on to the realm's other towns, and takes one in, at a fraction of the usual rate. Every realm keeps its gates open by custom; only a ruler who proclaims it shuts them.)

open.label: Gates open
open.desc: Trade and travellers come and go, and the sickness with them.

quarantine.label: Quarantine
quarantine.desc: A town with sickness going round shuts its gates: hardly a case gets in or out. Merchants and the shut-in grumble.
